name: Alcohol use disorder
course: Review the past 12 months and earlier drinking history; a 28-day diary cannot replace that history.

checklist.label: Pattern and intended limits
checklist.question: How does drinking fit into a usual week, and when does it go beyond what you planned?

checklist.label: Craving and attempts to change
checklist.question: What happens when you decide to drink less?

checklist.label: Consequences and priorities
checklist.question: Which responsibilities or relationships have changed around drinking?

checklist.label: Last drink and withdrawal history
checklist.question: When was your last drink, and what has happened when you stopped before?

checklist.label: Mood, other substances and safety
checklist.question: What else are you taking, and how do your mood and safety change with alcohol?

differentials: Risky drinking without established use disorder
Mood or anxiety symptoms with an independent or alcohol-related course

test.name: AUDIT-C
test.purpose: Brief adult screen for unhealthy drinking, followed by assessment of alcohol-use symptoms.
test.interpretation: A positive screen calls for further evaluation; it does not establish alcohol use disorder. Youth require an age-appropriate approach.

cautions: Seizures, marked confusion or severe withdrawal require urgent medical assessment. Do not simulate advice to stop heavy prolonged drinking abruptly or infer a disorder from quantity alone.

sources.title: NIAAA — Alcohol use disorder: from risk to diagnosis to recovery
NIAAA — Screen and assess: use quick, effective methods

name: Cannabis use disorder
course: Review use and consequences over the past 12 months; separate the longer pattern from effects during use or after cutting down.

checklist.label: Products, frequency and change
checklist.question: What cannabis products do you use, and how has that changed?

checklist.label: Control and craving
checklist.question: What happens when you try to delay or reduce cannabis?

checklist.label: Activities and functioning
checklist.question: Has using cannabis changed school, work, relationships or activities you value?

checklist.label: Timing of mental and sleep changes
checklist.question: How do anxiety, sleep or unusual experiences relate to using or stopping?

checklist.label: Hazardous situations and co-use
checklist.question: Have there been situations where cannabis or other substances made staying safe harder?

differentials: Independent anxiety, psychotic or sleep condition

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag cannabis-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Youth need confidential, developmentally appropriate assessment. Cannabis exposure alone is not a diagnosis; do not assume it explains every mood or perceptual symptom.

sources.title: CDC — Understanding your risk for cannabis use disorder
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening
APA — What is a substance use disorder?

name: Opioid use disorder
course: Assess problematic behavior within the past-year window, including prescribed and nonprescribed exposure.

checklist.label: Pain treatment and source
checklist.question: What are you taking for pain or other reasons, and how does actual use compare with the plan?

checklist.label: Control over use
checklist.question: What happens when you intend to take less or wait longer?

checklist.label: Time and consequences
checklist.question: How much of your day is shaped by getting, using or recovering from opioids?

checklist.label: Supervised dependence versus disorder
checklist.question: Which effects appeared during prescribed treatment, and what other problems occurred?

checklist.label: Overdose and sedative co-use
checklist.question: Have there been episodes of being hard to wake, and what other medicines or substances were involved?

differentials: Physical dependence during appropriate medical treatment
Undertreated pain or another substance-use condition

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag opioid-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Tolerance and withdrawal during solely appropriate medical supervision do not by themselves count toward opioid use disorder. Slow breathing or reduced consciousness is an emergency; do not offer dose or detox instructions.

sources.title: CDC — Opioid use disorder: diagnosis
CDC — Save a life from prescription opioid overdose
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening

name: Stimulant use disorder
course: Map use, impaired control and consequences over the past 12 months, including periods before use and during recovery.

checklist.label: Stimulant and treatment context
checklist.question: Which stimulants are involved, and which are prescribed?

checklist.label: Craving and limits
checklist.question: When have you used differently from what you planned?

checklist.label: Use, sleep and recovery cycle
checklist.question: How do sleep, energy and mood change while using and afterward?

checklist.label: Daily functioning
checklist.question: What has happened to work, school or relationships around this pattern?

checklist.label: Physical and mental warning signs
checklist.question: Have there been chest symptoms, overheating, confusion or frightening perceptions?

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag stimulant-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Chest pain, severe overheating, seizure or marked confusion calls for urgent medical assessment. A prescription for ADHD does not establish a use disorder.

sources.title: CDC — Stimulants
APA — What is a substance use disorder?
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening

name: Sedative, hypnotic, or anxiolytic use disorder
course: Review the past 12 months, including the original prescription, subsequent use pattern and timing of dose reductions or interruptions.

checklist.label: Medication and actual use
checklist.question: Which sleep or anxiety medicines do you take, and how does your use compare with the prescription?

checklist.label: Control and attempts to change
checklist.question: What has happened when you tried to follow a lower amount or reduce use?

checklist.label: Function and adverse consequences
checklist.question: Have memory, alertness, falls or responsibilities changed?

checklist.label: Withdrawal and interruption
checklist.question: What happened when a supply ran out or a dose changed?

checklist.label: Alcohol and opioid combination
checklist.question: What other medicines, alcohol or drugs do you sometimes take at the same time?

differentials: Expected physical dependence during prescribed treatment

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag sedative-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Physical dependence is not synonymous with addiction. Abrupt benzodiazepine reduction may cause life-threatening withdrawal; seizures or severe confusion need urgent medical care. No taper schedules are supplied.

sources.title: FDA — Benzodiazepine boxed warning, dependence and withdrawal
APA — What is a substance use disorder?
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening

name: Tobacco use disorder
course: Review nicotine use, changes and quit attempts over the past 12 months; distinguish withdrawal symptoms from baseline anxiety or poor concentration.

checklist.label: Nicotine products and routines
checklist.question: Which tobacco or nicotine products are part of your day?

checklist.label: Urges and triggers
checklist.question: When are urges hardest to manage?

checklist.label: Attempts to reduce
checklist.question: What happened the last time you tried to cut down or stop?

checklist.label: Symptoms when use is delayed
checklist.question: What changes in sleep, mood or concentration appear when you cannot use nicotine?

checklist.label: Consequences and personal priorities
checklist.question: How has nicotine affected your health, spending or activities you care about?

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag tobacco/nicotine-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Include vaping and smokeless products; quantity alone is insufficient. Adult screening guidance should not be copied uncritically to children or adolescents.

sources.title: CDC — Why quitting smoking is hard
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening

name: Gambling disorder
course: Explore a recurrent past-year pattern, with separate assessment of gambling limited to a manic episode.

checklist.label: Time, money and control
checklist.question: What does a typical gambling session look like, and how often does it exceed your plan?

checklist.label: Response to losses
checklist.question: What tends to happen after a loss?

checklist.label: Financial and relationship harm
checklist.question: What bills, relationships or responsibilities have been affected?

checklist.label: Concealment and support
checklist.question: How easy is it to talk about gambling and seek support?

checklist.label: Mood course and immediate safety
checklist.question: Does gambling change during unusually energized periods, and have losses left you feeling unsafe?

differentials: Other addictive behavior or substance use

test.name: Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI)
test.purpose: Structure discussion of gambling-related harm.
test.interpretation: A harm screen, not a stand-alone DSM diagnosis. This app does not administer its items or calculate its score.

cautions: Assess distress, self-harm risk and affected dependents without moral judgment. Financial loss alone does not establish the disorder.

sources.title: APA — What is gambling disorder?
NICE NG248 — Gambling-related harms: recommendations

name: Schizophrenia
course: Establish at least six months of overall disturbance, with the active symptom period and treatment-related exceptions assessed separately.

checklist.label: Perception and beliefs
checklist.question: What experiences have felt unusual or difficult to explain?

checklist.label: Thinking and communication change
checklist.question: Has it become harder to organize your thoughts or explain them to people?

checklist.label: Change from earlier functioning
checklist.question: What has changed in your routines, motivation or relationships?

checklist.label: Active and quieter periods
checklist.question: When did changes begin, and were there stretches when they eased?

checklist.label: Mood, substances and medical causes
checklist.question: How do these experiences relate to mood episodes, sleep, medicines or physical illness?

test.name: SCID-5 clinical interview
test.purpose: Clinician-led differential assessment of psychotic symptoms and their longitudinal course.
test.interpretation: Requires trained administration and appropriate materials; this educational checklist is not SCID and produces no diagnostic score.

cautions: Seek prompt assessment for new psychosis; urgent danger or inability to meet basic needs takes priority. Do not equate schizophrenia with violence or dissociative identity disorder.

sources.title: APA — What is schizophrenia? Related psychotic conditions
NIMH — Understanding psychosis
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Schizophreniform disorder
course: A schizophrenia-like episode lasts at least one month but less than six months; reassessment is needed as its course becomes clear.

checklist.label: Dated onset and duration
checklist.question: What was the first clear change, and when did it happen?

checklist.label: Psychotic experiences and organization
checklist.question: Which experiences or changes in thinking have been hardest to manage?

checklist.label: Baseline and current function
checklist.question: How are daily activities different from before this started?

checklist.label: Mood versus psychosis timeline
checklist.question: Do unusual experiences occur when your mood feels usual too?

checklist.label: Substances, sleep and medical history
checklist.question: What medication, substance, sleep or health changes happened around the onset?

differentials: Schizophrenia if sufficient course is established

test.name: SCID-5 clinical interview
test.purpose: Clinician-led differential assessment of psychosis with explicit duration review.
test.interpretation: Requires trained administration and appropriate materials; this educational checklist is not SCID and produces no diagnostic score.

cautions: Functional decline is clinically relevant but is not required in the same way as schizophrenia. Do not predict eventual schizophrenia from a short simulation.

sources.title: APA — What is schizophrenia? Related psychotic conditions
SAMHSA — DSM-IV to DSM-5 psychotic disorders comparison
NIMH — Understanding psychosis
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Brief psychotic disorder
course: Psychosis lasts at least one day and less than one month, followed by full return to prior functioning; incomplete recovery leaves the formulation provisional.

checklist.label: Sudden change and trigger context
checklist.question: What happened around the day these experiences began?

checklist.label: Nature of the episode
checklist.question: What did you notice in your perceptions, beliefs or ability to communicate?

checklist.label: Duration and return to baseline
checklist.question: When did it stop, and what is still different from before?

checklist.label: Relationship to mood episodes
checklist.question: Were there sustained periods of very high or very low mood?

checklist.label: Medical and exposure review
checklist.question: Were there illnesses, medication changes, substances or severe sleep loss?

test.name: SCID-5 clinical interview
test.purpose: Clinician-led differential assessment of brief psychosis, recovery and exclusions.
test.interpretation: Requires trained administration and appropriate materials; this educational checklist is not SCID and produces no diagnostic score.

cautions: Do not label an ongoing episode as fully recovered or infer a psychotic disorder from culturally accepted experiences. New psychosis warrants prompt clinical assessment.

sources.title: APA — What is schizophrenia? Related psychotic conditions
SAMHSA — DSM-IV to DSM-5 psychotic disorders comparison
NIMH — Understanding psychosis
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Delusional disorder
course: Evaluate a sustained belief-related disturbance for at least one month and its relationship to other psychotic or mood symptoms.

checklist.label: Belief, meaning and certainty
checklist.question: What has led you to this understanding, and how certain do you feel?

checklist.label: Cultural and shared context
checklist.question: How would people in your community understand this experience?

checklist.label: Behavior and function around belief
checklist.question: How has this concern changed what you do day to day?

checklist.label: Broader symptoms and mood
checklist.question: What other unusual experiences or mood changes have occurred?

checklist.label: Course and medical explanations
checklist.question: When did this begin, and what health or substance changes were happening then?

differentials: Culturally shared beliefs or accurate concerns

test.name: SCID-5 clinical interview
test.purpose: Clinician-led differential assessment of belief-related symptoms in cultural context.
test.interpretation: Requires trained administration and appropriate materials; this educational checklist is not SCID and produces no diagnostic score.

cautions: An interviewer cannot declare a concern false without evidence. Clarify respectfully without endorsing or arguing; assess risk arising from actions connected to the belief.

sources.title: APA — What is schizophrenia? Related psychotic conditions
SAMHSA — DSM-IV to DSM-5 psychotic disorders comparison
NIMH — Understanding psychosis
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Schizoaffective disorder
course: Map the entire illness: psychosis occurs with a major mood episode, at least two weeks of delusions/hallucinations occur without a major mood episode, and mood episodes occupy most of the active/residual course.

checklist.label: Psychotic symptom periods
checklist.question: When have voices, perceptions or beliefs been especially different?

checklist.label: Distinct depressive or manic episodes
checklist.question: Which periods of depression or unusually increased energy clearly differed from your usual self?

checklist.label: Psychosis outside mood episodes
checklist.question: Were there at least two weeks of these experiences when no major mood episode was present?

checklist.label: Relative duration across the illness
checklist.question: Across the whole illness, how much time involved a major mood episode?

checklist.label: Records, medical and exposure context
checklist.question: Which records or people could clarify the timeline, and what medicines or substances were involved?

differentials: Bipolar or depressive disorder when psychosis occurs only within mood episodes
Schizophrenia when mood episodes occupy only a minority of the course

test.name: SCID-5 clinical interview
test.purpose: Clinician-led differential assessment of the mood–psychosis timeline with collateral records.
test.interpretation: Requires trained administration and appropriate materials; this educational checklist is not SCID and produces no diagnostic score.

cautions: Simultaneous low mood and hallucinations are insufficient. If the longitudinal timing is missing, retain uncertainty rather than awarding a diagnosis.

sources.title: APA — What is schizophrenia? Related psychotic conditions
Malaspina et al. — Schizoaffective disorder in the DSM-5
SAMHSA — DSM-IV to DSM-5 psychotic disorders comparison
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Delirium
course: Acute change over hours or days with fluctuations from baseline; obtain collateral because the person's account may vary.

checklist.label: Acute departure from baseline
checklist.question: To the caregiver: what was different from their usual state, and when did it start?

checklist.label: Fluctuating attention and alertness
checklist.question: Does their ability to follow conversation or stay alert change through the day?

checklist.label: Possible acute medical trigger
checklist.question: What illness, pain, dehydration or recent procedure has occurred?

checklist.label: Medication and withdrawal context
checklist.question: Which medicines or substances changed recently?

checklist.label: Quiet as well as agitated changes
checklist.question: Have they become unusually sleepy, withdrawn or slow, even without agitation?

differentials: Dementia, including delirium superimposed on dementia
Other acute neurological or medical illness

test.name: 4AT
test.purpose: Rapid clinician assessment for possible delirium in appropriate settings.
test.interpretation: A suggestive result requires clinical diagnosis and cause assessment. NICE specifies CAM-ICU or ICDSC in critical care/recovery settings; no score is inferred from chat.

cautions: This is an urgent medical-assessment scenario, not routine outpatient diagnostic practice. A quiet presentation can still be serious; address delirium first when dementia and delirium are hard to distinguish.

sources.title: NICE CG103 — Delirium: assessment and diagnosis recommendations
4AT developers — Rapid clinical test for delirium detection

name: Mild neurocognitive disorder
course: Establish acquired decline from an earlier baseline while independence is largely retained, sometimes through extra effort or aids.

checklist.label: Change in cognitive abilities
checklist.question: What thinking or memory tasks feel different from a year or two ago?

checklist.label: Independence and compensations
checklist.question: Which tasks can you still manage yourself, and what reminders or strategies help?

checklist.label: Corroboration
checklist.question: Who has noticed the changes, and what examples could they share?

checklist.label: Onset and progression
checklist.question: Did this develop gradually, suddenly or in steps?

checklist.label: Mood, sensory and medical context
checklist.question: How are sleep, mood, hearing, vision and medicines affecting these tasks?

differentials: Major neurocognitive disorder with lost independence

test.name: Cognitive assessment with an appropriate brief screen and neuropsychological follow-up
test.purpose: Compare objective cognition, prior abilities and real-world independence.
test.interpretation: Brief screens such as Mini-Cog can flag concern but cannot alone determine diagnosis or cause. Use suitable language, sensory accommodations and norms; do not invent scores.

cautions: Do not equate older age, forgetfulness or mild cognitive impairment terminology automatically with a DSM diagnosis or Alzheimer's disease.

sources.title: APA — Mild neurocognitive disorder fact sheet
NIA — Assessing cognitive impairment in older patients

name: Major neurocognitive disorder
course: Acquired cognitive decline interferes with everyday independence; document the baseline, progression and likely cause.

checklist.label: Affected cognitive abilities
checklist.question: Which thinking, memory, language or planning tasks have become difficult?

checklist.label: Loss of independence
checklist.question: What tasks now need another person's help that did not before?

checklist.label: Gradual versus sudden change
checklist.question: When did changes begin, and how have they progressed?

checklist.label: Collateral and current safety
checklist.question: What has a trusted person noticed about medicines, money, travel or home safety?

checklist.label: Potential contributors and acute change
checklist.question: Were there recent illnesses, medication changes or sudden episodes of confusion?

differentials: Delirium or delirium superimposed on dementia
Different neurological causes of cognitive decline

test.name: Comprehensive cognitive and functional assessment
test.purpose: Combine direct testing, informant history, examination and cause investigation.
test.interpretation: An AD8 or Mini-Cog may support detection; no single score establishes dementia or its subtype. The simulator supplies no physical examination or biomarker result.

cautions: Dementia is not inevitable ageing. Sudden deterioration requires medical assessment; obtain consent-sensitive collateral and respect retained abilities.

sources.title: APA — Dementia and Alzheimer's disease
NIA — Assessing cognitive impairment in older patients

name: Borderline personality disorder
course: Establish a longstanding pattern across relationships and settings, not a diagnosis based on one crisis or several simulated days.

checklist.label: Relationships and separation
checklist.question: What tends to happen when an important relationship feels uncertain?

checklist.label: Emotion changes and recovery
checklist.question: How do strong feelings build and settle, and what tends to set them off?

checklist.label: Self-image and direction
checklist.question: Does your sense of who you are or what matters to you change at difficult times?

checklist.label: Coping, impulsivity and safety
checklist.question: When overwhelmed, what do you do to cope, and have you felt at risk of harming yourself?

checklist.label: Pattern versus mood episode
checklist.question: Has this pattern appeared for years, or mainly in distinct episodes of unusually high energy or depression?

test.name: SCID-5-PD
test.purpose: Assess enduring personality patterns in a clinician-led interview.
test.interpretation: Licensed interview with trained clinical judgment; these practice prompts are not its items or scoring system.

cautions: Use nonjudgmental language and assess safety directly. Adolescent diagnosis needs persistent evidence and specialist developmental assessment; do not call distress manipulative.

sources.title: NIMH — Borderline personality disorder
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Avoidant personality disorder
course: Explore an enduring, widespread pattern from earlier life, rather than recent anxiety or ordinary introversion.

checklist.label: Avoidance across settings
checklist.question: Which situations do you hold back from, and what do you expect might happen?

checklist.label: Self-view and rejection
checklist.question: How do you imagine other people see you?

checklist.label: Desired relationships
checklist.question: What connections would you want if fear of criticism were less strong?

checklist.label: Persistence and cost
checklist.question: How long has this pattern affected relationships, school or work?

test.name: SCID-5-PD
test.purpose: Assess enduring personality patterns in a clinician-led interview.
test.interpretation: Licensed interview with trained clinical judgment; these practice prompts are not its items or scoring system.

cautions: Check actual bullying, exclusion and cultural context. Shyness or preference for solitude is insufficient; childhood patterns need developmental interpretation.

sources.title: APA — What are personality disorders?
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder
course: Look for persistent inflexibility across contexts and earlier life, with consequences beyond a single demanding period.

checklist.label: Standards and completion
checklist.question: When does getting things just right make it difficult to finish?

checklist.label: Flexibility and delegation
checklist.question: What happens when someone does a task differently from your approach?

checklist.label: Work, leisure and relationship cost
checklist.question: How do rules or work priorities affect time with other people?

checklist.label: Longstanding pattern versus intrusive rituals
checklist.question: Has this long felt like your usual approach, or are there unwanted thoughts and rituals you feel driven to neutralize?

test.name: SCID-5-PD
test.purpose: Assess enduring personality patterns in a clinician-led interview.
test.interpretation: Licensed interview with trained clinical judgment; these practice prompts are not its items or scoring system.

cautions: OCPD differs from OCD. High standards, culturally valued diligence or temporary work pressure alone do not establish a personality disorder.

sources.title: APA — What are personality disorders?
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Gender dysphoria
course: Assess persistence, distress and functioning over at least six months using developmentally appropriate child or adolescent/adult criteria.

checklist.label: Person's own language and goals
checklist.question: What name and language feel right for you, and what would you like help with?

checklist.label: Specific distress rather than identity
checklist.question: Which experiences with your body or how others see you cause distress, if any?

checklist.label: Developmental timing
checklist.question: When did these concerns become important, and how have they changed with development?

checklist.label: Function and social context
checklist.question: How does this affect daily life, and what part comes from how other people treat you?

checklist.label: Safety, strengths and support
checklist.question: Where do you feel accepted and safe, and what support would help?

differentials: Gender diversity without clinically significant dysphoria
Distress related to discrimination or rejection
Co-occurring depression, anxiety or body-image concerns

test.name: Developmentally appropriate clinical assessment of gender-related distress
test.purpose: Clarify the person's experience, persistence, impairment and support needs.
test.interpretation: No identity test establishes a disorder. Evaluate distress in context; this checklist cannot diagnose or determine a treatment pathway.

cautions: Transgender or gender-diverse identity is not itself a disorder. Pronouns, clothing or interests do not establish dysphoria. Avoid assumptions about puberty, anatomy or desired outcomes.

sources.title: APA — What is gender dysphoria?

name: Complex PTSD — ICD-11 comparison
course: Use ICD-11: establish trauma-related PTSD features plus persistent difficulties in emotion regulation, self-view and relationships, with functional impact.

checklist.label: Trauma context and permission
checklist.question: Without details you do not want to share, what experience still affects you?

checklist.label: Re-experiencing, avoidance and threat
checklist.question: What reminders bring the experience into the present, and what do you avoid or stay alert for?

checklist.label: Regulating emotion
checklist.question: What happens when feelings become intense or shut down?

checklist.label: Self-view and relationships
checklist.question: How has this affected how you see yourself and feel close to people?

checklist.label: Persistence and impairment
checklist.question: How long have these difficulties affected daily life, and what still helps?

differentials: ICD-11 PTSD without additional self-organization difficulties

test.name: International Trauma Questionnaire (ITQ)
test.purpose: Self-report assessment of ICD-11 PTSD and complex PTSD features and impairment.
test.interpretation: Supports a provisional formulation, not a definitive diagnosis. Use an appropriate age/language version; no ITQ score is derived from these practice prompts.

cautions: CPTSD is a separate ICD-11 diagnosis, not a separate DSM-5-TR diagnosis. Repeated trauma alone is insufficient; avoid forcing a detailed trauma narrative.

sources.title: VA National Center for PTSD — Complex PTSD: history and definitions
VA National Center for PTSD — International Trauma Questionnaire

name: Gaming disorder — ICD-11 comparison
course: ICD-11 normally requires an impairing pattern over at least 12 months; use the full ICD-11 requirements when considering exceptions.

checklist.label: Control of gaming
checklist.question: What happens when you plan to end a gaming session?

checklist.label: Competing priorities
checklist.question: Which activities or responsibilities have gaming displaced?

checklist.label: Continuation despite harm
checklist.question: What problems have you noticed, and how has gaming changed since then?

checklist.label: Duration and functional impact
checklist.question: For how long has this pattern affected school, work, relationships or health?

checklist.label: Context and alternative explanations
checklist.question: What do gaming and your online community provide, and what else is affecting your life?

differentials: Gaming as coping with depression or anxiety
Gambling behavior involving bets or stakes

test.name: Structured ICD-11 gaming assessment
test.purpose: Assess control, priority, persistence despite consequences and significant impairment.
test.interpretation: Hours played alone are not diagnostic. This is an educational interview framework, not a validated scored instrument.

cautions: Keep ICD-11 gaming disorder distinct from DSM-5-TR Internet Gaming Disorder, a condition for further study. Interpret youth routines and family conflict developmentally.

sources.title: WHO — Addictive behaviours: gaming disorder
APA — Internet gaming
